title: [Feature Request] Multi-map Compare Mode (Side-by-Side View)
body:
# [Feature Request] Multi-map Compare Mode (Side-by-Side View)

## Overview

One of the important user needs is the ability to compare multiple indicators simultaneously by viewing them in separate, synchronized map windows — not overlaid on the same map. This helps analysts and decision-makers understand complex multi-dimensional situations, e.g. where regions have low access to schools, low access to health facilities, AND high population density, all visible at once without switching views.

The objective of this ticket is to introduce a new **Multi-map Compare Mode** that allows users to view up to **6 indicator layers side by side**, each rendered in its own independent map window, all synchronized in terms of extent, zoom, basemap, and time settings.

> **Note:** This is based on the Swipe Mode feature request (see #37), which splits a single map view with a draggable bar. This feature renders fully independent map windows placed next to each other.

---

## Current State

The existing Compare Mode supports:
- **Outline & Fill Mode** — two layers are overlaid on the same map using outlines and fill colours.

This new feature request (#37) will support:
- **Swipe Mode** — a single map is split by a vertical bar, showing one layer on each side.

Both modes are limited to **2 layers** and operate within a **single map viewport**. Users who want to compare three or more indicators can currently rely on filters or composite indicator layers, but there is no way to view them simultaneously.


---

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a new compare mode: **"Side-by-Side View"**, accessible from the existing compare mode dropdown. When activated:

- The main map viewport splits into **multiple equally-sized map windows** arranged in a responsive grid.
- Each window renders **one selected indicator layer** independently, sharing the same basemap, bounding box, zoom level, admin level, and time configuration.
- Up to **6 layers** can be selected for comparison.
- All map win

title: [Feature Request] Add create endpoint for dashboards in API v1
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Yes. API v1 can list and retrieve dashboards, but it cannot create them.
This forces teams to use the UI for creation, which blocks full API-based workflows.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add `POST /api/v1/dashboards/` to API v1 and reuse the existing dashboard creation flow.

Requirements:
- Accept dashboard definition JSON in the payload.
- Allow only authenticated users with at least creator role.
- Deny anonymous/public and non-creator users.
- Support JSON and multipart requests (including optional icon upload).
- Return `201` on success and `400` with clear validation errors on bad input.
- Keep creation transaction-safe (no partial save if relation save fails).
- Update API docs to match actual request/response behavior.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Keep creation UI-only. This does not support API automation.
- Build a separate API-only create flow. This can drift from existing UI logic.
- Redesign the payload model first. This increases scope and delays delivery.

**Additional context**
Maintainer note:
- Dashboard definition is already JSON, so posting JSON should be enough for create.
- This endpoint must not be available to public users.
- Minimum role should be creator.

Scope:
- Add create support to the v1 dashboards endpoint.
- Reuse existing dashboard creation flow.
- Add tests for success, permission denial, validation errors, multipart upload, and transaction rollback.
- Update API docs/schema for create.

Out of scope:
- Update or patch semantics.
- Full payload redesign.
- Unrelated dashboard feature or permission changes.
- Generic map viewer flow where users add layers and save config as URL (future work).

- [ ] `POST /api/v1/dashboards/` is available in API v1.
- [ ] Endpoint requires authentication and creator+ role.

body:

The current landing page presents an overview and a sortable, searchable list of projects - including 1) for logged users: the user’s own projects and projects created and shared by others, and 2) for public users: publicly shared projects. title: [Feature Request] Collect and visualize usage statistics
body:
# Problem
Our web-based geospatial platform currently lacks usage monitoring and analytics capabilities. Without usage statistics, we have limited insight into how users interact with the platform, which features are most utilized, and potential performance bottlenecks. Implementing usage tracking will enable the team to make data-driven decisions for feature improvements, resource allocation, and overall platform optimization.


# Solution
Provide super admin and content owners with the statistics on individual items usage and other usage statistics.

Statistics are mainly needed for:
- [ ] Projects (e.g. number of views)
- [ ] Indicators (e.g. number of requests for data, for which datasets / countries / dates)
- [ ] Users activities: number of logins,
- [ ] ...?

Other considerations, e.g.:
- User Activity Metrics:
  - Daily/weekly/monthly active users (DAU/WAU/MAU).
  - Number of logins per user.
  - User session duration.
  - Frequency of platform visits.
- Performance Metrics
  - Response time of key views and endpoints.
  - Average load time of maps and data layers.
  - Error rates or failed API calls.
- User Segmentation
  - Usage patterns by user role (e.g., admin vs. viewer).


# Implementation Suggestions:
## Django Middleware for Basic Tracking:
Log each request with timestamp, user ID (if authenticated), URL path, and response time.
Store logs in a database table or external logging service (e.g., ELK, Grafana Loki).

Track specific events (e.g., map viewed, layer added, export triggered).
Emit signals on important user actions to capture detailed context.

title: [Feature Request] Expand Support for Uploading Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG)
body:
# Current State
Our web-based GIS platform (GeoSight) currently supports user-uploaded context layers stored directly in the platform database as "cloud native GIS layers." At the moment, the upload interface only supports vector format, i.e. zipped Shapefiles (.shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj in a zip archive). These layers are then stored in PostGIS and made available for use in map dashboards.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01e367c0-3cc2-4bb1-8f04-e9113d7a7619)

Many datasets in weather, climate science, and Earth observation are distributed as rasters - gridded data where each cell (pixel) contains a value like temperature, precipitation, vegetation index, or satellite reflectance. These datasets are:
- Large in size (often hundreds of MBs to several GBs)
- Spatio-temporal (covering wide areas across time)
- Frequently updated (e.g., daily satellite passes, hourly forecasts)

Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) are a modern raster format that enables fast, scalable access to large geospatial datasets—such as satellite imagery and climate grids—directly over HTTP, making them ideal for web-based Earth observation and GIS applications.

# Problem
Our current implementation allow users to create COG-based context layers [1] using external, publicly available COGs [2] by referencing their URLs [3]. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043edc95-b116-424b-a0fb-a3e7878f9636)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f90e48cb-31fe-4cd6-ab7b-5a3f3b4b1bc0)


## Limitations of current approach
- No control over data availability: external COGs may be deleted, or moved by the host, which breaks dashboards or layers without warning.
- Inability to upload our own COG files: users can't directly use internally generated raster data, which blocks use cases like processed satellite imagery, terrain models, or climate simulations.

title: Implement Dynamic H3 Binning for Cloud Native Point Layers
body:
## Problem
GeoSight supports uploading point Cloud Native layers (e.g. in a shapefile format). Currently, styling of Cloud Native GIS layers is based on [Mapbox Style Spec](https://docs.mapbox.com/style-spec/reference/layers/) and requires customizing style JSON file [2]. Users can also use a built-in [Maputnik](https://github.com/maplibre/maputnik) style editor [1].

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19ecc04d-2d75-4fea-9514-a3fb4cd11f23)

Binning point layers into H3 hexagons enables clearer visualization of spatial patterns, especially in dense or overlapping datasets. It improves performance for large datasets, supports multiscale analysis, and avoids issues tied to arbitrary administrative boundaries by offering a consistent spatial unit across zoom levels.


## Solution
Enable users to apply dynamic H3 binning to uploaded Cloud Native point layers within the platform, transforming raw point data into aggregated hexagonal grids using the H3 spatial index. Implementation would involve computing H3 indices for each point at the chosen resolution and aggregating values (e.g. count, sum, average) within each hex cell. Users will be able to specify aggregation method (count, sum, max etc) as well as coloring style (continuous or stepped classes) and the Mapbox Style JSON code will update automatically to reflect the selection.

- [ ] Allow users to dynamically aggregate and visualize point data (e.g., schools, clinics, facilities) into H3 hexagons at a user-selected resolution.
- [ ] Support on-the-fly heatmapping or statistical aggregation (e.g., count, average, sum) via the user interface or API.

title: Add Support for H3 Hexagonal Indexing of Indicator Data
body:
## Description  
Currently, GeoSight supports Indicator Data referenced to predefined administrative boundaries (e.g., states, districts, provinces). 

We propose adding support for [H3](https://h3geo.org/) — a hierarchical hexagonal spatial indexing system — to enhance the platform’s spatial analysis capabilities beyond static admin boundaries. 

Implementing support for the H3 dynamic hexagonal grid reference system in our web GIS mapping platform is important because grid-based mapping mitigates issues associated with using administrative boundaries—such as the need for preloading administrative boundary datasets, inconsistent admin boundary sizes and shapes, different administrative levels, political sensitivities as well as changes over time—by providing a uniform, resolution-adjustable spatial framework for more accurate and comparable geospatial analysis. Additionally, H3 indexing does not require preloading shapefiles / geometries for specific areas, as H3 tiles can be generated on the fly for any Area Of Interest.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddb480e8-1e5f-4d24-8855-068101166327)

## Proposed Functionality  
1. **Storage of Data by H3 Tiles**  
   - Enable the platform to store Indicator Data (e.g., number of schools, number of children with limited access to health services etc) georeferenced to H3 hexagons instead of administrative boundaries. 
   - Allow importing Indicator Data referenced to H3 tiles (each observation value must be associated with a specific H3 tile ID, rather than admin boundary code, such as ZIP Code, Pcode etc).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc50d988-7f79-4c3f-a596-059c54b83bf7)

2. **Visualization of Data by H3 Tiles**  
   - Allow adding Indicator Layers in Projects/Dashboards based on H3 tiles, rather than based on admin boundary reference layers

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16a28539-2700-498e-b22e-86c5dc229e47)

title: Add GeoAI Assistant to allow querying, analyzing and visualizing Google Earth Engine datasets
body:
## Problem
Spatial data analysis is essential for decision-making in humanitarian and development contexts, e.g. for disaster preparedness and response, designing programs and interventions or identifying vulnerable populations at risk. However, accessing and utilizing geospatial datasets from platforms like Google Earth Engine (GEE) often requires technical expertise in querying and processing spatial data. This creates a barrier for users who lack advanced GIS knowledge, limiting their ability to leverage powerful geospatial insights.


## Solution
GeoSight - our web mapping application, powered by Django, PostGIS, and MapLibre, needs an intuitive solution that enables users to interact with geospatial data using natural language. By integrating a GeoAI assistant, users can easily discover and add datasets from GEE, perform spatial analyses such as zonal statistics, and aggregate results at administrative levels (e.g., districts) without requiring complex scripting. This functionality will enhance accessibility, improve decision-making, and streamline geospatial analysis workflows for a broader audience.

title: Limits System and API
body:
We need a system for limits. Limits are quota's that define how many of a given resource an organisation (see https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/issues/217) may have. Things that may be limited:

* Number of users for the organisation
* Number of projects for the organisation
* Number of and storage space occupied by related tables for the organisation
* Number of and storage space occupied by related indicator for the organisation
* Number of scheduled jobs for the organisation
* Which types of data importers can be used


By default, limits should be disabled for a deployment.
When limits are enabled, a new type of user 'platform manager' should be enabled. Platform managers can create or manage organisations and set limits.

The platform manager shall be able to issue themselves an API key that is used for managing the platform.

An API should allow a remote management interface to query and set the limits for a deployed instance.

title: Organisation support
body:
We need to implement support for multiple organisations. When establishing a new account, the user should join one or more organisations. We can provide an experience similar to Google, where the user account can be switched from one organisation to another e.g.  

![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/178003/914d2031-ee48-42d4-aca5-09800753ebe2)


However I think it would make more sense to follow our approach in BIMS (https://github.com/kartoza/django-bims/) whereby a user has a single account / profile, and can belong to multiple organisations. An organisation manager can invite new or existing users to their organisation. 

When a user with the needed permissions sets up a new organisation, they should provide a domain/ subdomain that will be linked to that organisation profile.

Opening the site at a given organisation's subdomain will 'activate' that organisation such that:

* only users who have been added to that organisation will be able to log in
* only projects, that have been created under the organisation will be listed
* all resources will be filtered, such that only resources associated with the organisation will be shown
* any branding, colours and organisation titling etc. will be shown

We should be careful to ensure that data from one organisation cannot 'leak' to another organisation. If there are specific use cases for sharing data between organisations makes sense, we should define and agree these carefully.

title: Support user uploaded boundaries
body:
We would like to be able to create projects where the administration boundaries are provided by the project owner.

The functionality should support popular geospatial file formats such as:

* geojson
* geopackage
* geoparquet
* shapefile

Upon uploading the dataset, the user should indicate columns that correspond to:

* Boundary level
* Boundary name
* Boundary unique code

Conceivably we could support multiple layers (e.g. admin0, admin1) to represent different administration levels, or we could require a single layer which contains different admin levels codified by their 'Boundary level' column to indicate which level they represent.

Additionally, it would be good to store a reference for the layer such that the boundaries can be cited if needed.

Internally we should load the user uploaded boundaries into the postgresql backend and serve them back to the project as as_mvt vector tiles so they they are essentially the same delivery mechanism as pulling boundaries from GeoRepo.

Where Ucodes and other GeoRepo specific API calls, this GeoSight-side implementation should completely replace the need for GeoRepo, emulating the appropriate API calls if needed or providing an alternate logic path for ucode lookups etc.

title: [WIP] API Design
body:
# Overview

This issue describes a proposed API for GeoSight. What do we want to achieve
with the API? Some possibilities:

* ⬆️️ **Push data to GeoSight**
    * **Use case:** App integrations to push data from other places
    * Insert indicator values (already in swagger)
    * Replace related tables (in future replace / add partial data in the
      table)
* ⬇️ **Pull data from GeoSight**
    * **Use case:** Get data from GeoSight to display in 3rd party app
    * Lower priority than push?
* 🛠️ **GeoSight Content Management**
    * Configure projects etc.
    * **Use case:** Alternative management UI, focus on import / export actions which allow backing up, migrating, batch creation, integrations with SDMX etc.

Our API will address two areas on concern:

* data - these are actual information units used to drive the visualisation of the platform
 * indicator values - these are admin area / geography linked observations (indicator) for a specific date and time
 * related tables - these are detailed structured tables which allow the creation of 1:m relationships between indicator values and additional data associated with that indicator
* content - these are the declared indicators, projects, styles etc. that have been created on the system by our users (creators / content managers).

# API


## /api/v1/projects/

* 📒 Description:
    * A detailed definition of a project.
* ⬇️ Parameters:

In GeoSight, indicators can be of 3 types: 1) Integer, 2) Float, 3) Category. Type 1 and 2 are numbers, type 3 is string. From the dashboard view, users can download the data in Excel or GeoJSON formats:
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/547d154d-55e6-4f9c-8b04-ad3056bbe7aa)

When exporting to GeoJSON, all value in the Value column are represented as strings not numbers, thus cannot be directly used for visualization e.g. as a choropleth map in other GIS systems, e.g. in QGIS:

...

title: [Feature Request] Add indicators to landing page gallery
body:
## Problem

Over time when you gather up many projects, the return visit rate to projects may be low / sporadic. Finding ways to call user's attention to particular projects when there is "something to see" could be helpful in letting decision makers and maintainers hone in on key projects.


## Proposed solution

It would be nice to have a system of indicators on the  landing page where under different conditions, different indicators are displayed e.g.

![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/178003/38a6d576-062b-414a-ade7-17fc5b15d4a3)

1. **Key thresholds have been crossed** - e.g. if the number if displaced persons in a project's context layer has crossed a threshold, we put a badge on the gallery icon ⚠️
2. **Errors harvesting indicators** - if the updating of a project is failing, show a badge to let the project admin know there is something to investigate ⛔️

Over time we could add to the list of indicator types above if we think of more that are meaningful.

It would also be nice to be able to filter the projects by the indicators so that you could have a view of just projects where a threshold has been crossed.

title: [Feature Request] In the indicator layer config - add button to edit the selected style
body:
# Overview
When defining the style for an Indicator or when editing the style of an Indicator Layer in a Project, user can choose between different style types: 
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/0b541e2c-ab3d-4138-a612-a601d9966c5c)

Style can be created in a Style Library so that it can be reused (referenced) by many Indicators or Indicator Layers. If the style in the library is changed - all Indicators or Indicator Layers referencing this style will be updated on the map, as the style is dynamically pulled from the library.

When editing the style of an Indicator Layer in a Project, user may choose the style from the library, but may want to edit it (if he has permissions to edit a given style).


# Solution
Use case: a user opens config of the Indicator Layer in the Project. The Layer is using style from the library. The user wants to edit the style in the library.

- [ ] add a button to redirect the user to edit a style
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/79dc5a07-89ed-43ac-91e4-5b4f21705c6e)

The edit button / icon should redirect to `.../admin/style/4/edit` or open a popup window with the ability to edit this style. Once the style is modified and saved, the user should go back to the Indicator Layer config page within a Project config.

title: [Feature Request] Add another compare mode: swipe
body:
# Overview
One of the important user needs is the ability to compare multiple indicators at the same time. This helps understand complex situations, e.g. where children have low access to schools AND low access to health. The objective of this ticket is to introduce a new comparing mode, which will allow users to swipe between two different indicator layers, which is a common approach for comparing two map layers. As GeoSight uses [MapLibre ](https://maplibre.org/)web mapping library, we can reuse one of the existing implementations of the swipe tool (see links below).


# Current state
By default, only one indicator layer can be visualized at a time. Compare mode allows users to compare two indicator layers at a time. Currently, users can enable compare mode by clicking on the "compare" button in the map toolbar.
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/69fe3da0-ff22-4399-ba95-36740d42c498)

Once clicked, the radio buttons on the list of indicator layers will turn into checkboxes. The first selected layer will be visualized using thicker and color-coded outlines. 
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/120da395-0e49-45e7-ad1c-88d823e240c1)

When a user selects the second layer - it will be rendered below the outline layer and visualized using filled colors. Additionally, the second legend will display and both indicators will show up in the widgets (if enabled and configured to sync with the map indicators)
![image](https://github.com/unicef-drp/GeoSight-OS/assets/37516253/e7109dee-ab1d-4d55-9d68-ac377e64ac56)
